SLIIT Research Project / R26-IT-145

Smart Camp Box

An Integrated IoT and Artificial Intelligence Framework for Safety, Communication, Learning Assistance, and Resource Optimization in Disaster Relief Camps

A single portable, offline-first box that predicts flood risk at each camp, gates educational content for displaced children by psycho-attentional readiness, and keeps critical messages flowing over degraded networks.

02 / Domain

Research Context

Three operational failures persist in disaster relief camps — site-level hazard warnings, children's learning readiness, and reliable communication. The Smart Camp Box addresses all three from one platform.

Literature Survey Research Gap Research Problem Research Objectives Sub-Objectives Methodology Technologies Used

Literature Survey

Environmental risk monitoring. IoT sensor networks and GIS-based watershed analysis are well established for regional flood warning. However, most systems report district-level risk from accumulated rainfall rather than evaluating whether one specific camp location will be covered by rising water. Combining GPS-derived altitude with Digital Elevation Models for camp-level inundation checks remains underexplored.

Education in disaster contexts. Trauma-induced neurological suppression directly impairs children's attention, memory and academic learning. Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025) affected 890,000 children and damaged 1,682 schools with teacher-to-student ratios reaching 1:77 — yet no AI-driven educational system was part of the emergency response. Existing platforms assume the learner is psychologically ready.

IoT communication under constraint. MQTT is the dominant lightweight protocol for IoT, but standard deployments assign static QoS levels at configuration time. Uniform QoS in constrained gateways cannot distinguish life-critical biometric data from routine telemetry precisely when bandwidth collapses.

Research Gap

G1

Regional warnings, not site-specific risk

Existing monitoring systems stop at regional granularity — no unified platform fuses live telemetry, external river data, DEM terrain features and ML into a per-camp flood probability.

G2

Readiness is assumed, never measured

No educational system deployed in an emergency applies an automated, per-session psycho-attentional gate before delivering curriculum content, or monitors children for persistent welfare distress.

G3

Static QoS in dynamic degradation

MQTT QoS is fixed at configuration time. Nothing adapts message priority to real-time network state, so critical registration and distribution data can be lost under severe constraints.

Research Problem

Disaster relief camps face three persistent operational challenges simultaneously: camp-level flood prediction, psychological and attentional readiness assessment for displaced children, and resilient communication under degraded network conditions.

During Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025), 1.4 million people were displaced and floodwater forced 894 of 990 active relief camps to close. Current systems solve these challenges in isolation — and many depend on stable Internet connectivity that disaster environments cannot guarantee. The result is delayed evacuation decisions, ineffective educational delivery for traumatised learners, and loss of critical operational messages at the worst possible moment.

Research Objectives

To design, develop and evaluate the Smart Camp Box — a portable, offline-first IoT framework that tightly couples a location-aware environmental risk monitoring engine, the Psycho-Attentional Gated Educational System (PAGES), and the Semantic-Aware Adaptive Message Prioritization (SAAMP) framework with smart resource management into a single platform for disaster relief camp operations.

SDG 4 Target 4.5 · education in emergencies SDG 3 Target 3.4 · welfare monitoring SDG 11 Target 11.5 · disaster risk reduction SDG 9 Target 9.c · offline-first infrastructure

Sub-Objectives

SUB-SYSTEM 01

Location-Aware Risk Monitoring

Continuously assess flood risk at each individual camp in real time.

  • GPS/GNSS altitude + DEM risk profiling
  • Multi-sensor telemetry & watershed analysis
  • ML risk model with automated threshold alerts
  • Centralized multi-camp dashboard
SUB-SYSTEM 02

PAGES Learning Gate

Assess and support the cognitive readiness of Grade 3–4 children (ages 7–9) per session.

  • Three-source behavioural fusion scoring
  • Binary readiness gate with calming re-assessment
  • NIE-aligned content delivery
  • Two-phase welfare anomaly detection
SUB-SYSTEM 03

SAAMP & Smart Resource Management

Guarantee prioritized delivery of critical operational data and run fraud-free, predictive resource management on constrained networks.

  • Biometric registration & wristband identity
  • Source-Action criticality classification
  • Predictive network-state monitoring
  • Adaptive MQTT QoS + priority buffering
  • Entitlement-verified resource distribution
  • Resource demand prediction model

Methodology

Field & literature grounding

Design Science Research cycle: literature review across three domains plus stakeholder consultation — a field interview at the Kolonnawa Divisional Secretariat, an NDRSC senior field officer, and Homagama zonal education authorities on camp safety, resource allocation and children's education needs.

Build the sub-systems

Three tightly coupled modules — risk prediction, PAGES gating, and SAAMP message prioritization with smart resource management — developed in parallel by the three researchers.

Integrate on the box

Modules converge on Smart Camp Box hardware: ESP32 sensor node, Raspberry Pi 5 edge server, solar power, and MQTT bridging to the cloud dashboard.

Evaluate against targets

Flood classification reached 90.94% accuracy with under 9% false alerts on 25,000 records; the PAGES pilot covered 580 sessions with 29 children at 94.19% leave-one-out consistency; SAAMP sustained over 95% critical-message delivery with ~50% lower urgent latency under simulated degradation — all modules concurrently within a 1.2 s average task time.

03 / System Architecture

One Box, Three Layers

Camp admin, child users and edge sensors connect over the device's built-in local WiFi to three on-device modules, each backed by its own SQLite store. An MQTT bridge forwards local data through the EMQX broker into a cloud PostgreSQL layer powering anomaly detection, resource prediction and the administrative dashboard.

01 / Safety

Location-Aware Environmental Risk Monitoring

Hansana G.P · IT22064868

GPS/GNSS altitude and DEM integration combined with rainfall, soil moisture, ground movement and river-level data into a camp-specific flood prediction model with automated dashboard alerts.

90.94%
Classification accuracy
<9%

Evaluation records
Key objectives
  • GPS/GNSS location with latitude, longitude and altitude for elevation-based risk profiling.
  • Real-time rainfall intensity, soil moisture, ground movement and humidity at each camp.
  • Geospatial watershed and upstream-flow analysis via QGIS and OpenStreetMap.
  • External river-level, gauging-station and weather data with a proximity matcher.
  • Ten-feature vector fed to an Optuna-tuned, isotonic-calibrated XGBoost at 0.30, with SHAP explainability.
  • Cloud dashboard aggregating live risk across all registered camps.

Pipeline
01Sense GNSS altitude, rainfall, soil moisture and river level at the camp.
02Enrich with DEM terrain and QGIS watershed / upstream-flow features.
03Score flood probability on the edge with calibrated XGBoost + SHAP.
04Push threshold alerts to the centralized multi-camp dashboard.
02 / Learning

Psycho-Attentional Gated Educational System (PAGES)

Deerasinghe A D S N S · IT22065780

An offline-first application that measures a child's readiness through a gamified Go/No-Go task, gates curriculum content per session, and flags persistent welfare distress with ML anomaly detection.

94.19%
LOO consistency
580
Sessions · 29 children
0%
False-positive rate
Key objectives
  • Three-source behavioural fusion: gamified inhibitory-control task (50%), passive signals (30%) and rolling baseline (20%).
  • Binary readiness gate thresholded at 55/100 with calming breathing and re-assessment.
  • Standardized cognitive content aligned to the NIE Grade 3–4 curriculum.
  • Two-phase anomaly detection — Z-score from session three, then per-child Isolation Forest.
  • Welfare alerts on three consecutive flagged sessions, or three flags in the last five.
  • Full offline operation on Raspberry Pi 5 with dual-mode AP+STA Wi-Fi and cloud sync.
MERNFlaskscikit-learn SQLiteRaspberry Pi 5
Pipeline
01Run the gamified Go/No-Go task and fuse it with passive signals.
02Score 0–100 and gate content at the 55/100 readiness threshold.
03Deliver NIE Grade 3–4 content only when the child is ready.
04Flag persistent welfare distress with per-child anomaly detection.

Key objectives
  • Pre-disaster fingerprint registration (R307) with wristband barcode for duplication-free entitlements.
  • Source-Action Classification Schema assigning Critical / Important / Routine across six sources.
  • Real-time network monitor classifying connectivity as Good, Weak, Poor or Offline.
  • Random Forest predictor forecasting network quality 60 seconds ahead for proactive QoS.
  • Entitlement-verified resource distribution — wristband scans block duplicate issuance.
  • Supervised model forecasting daily food, water and medicine from demographics and flow.
